added_failures_note: both arms ran the same fifteen importing files with no new test in the base tree; base-suite.log reads '3 failed, 177 passed in 550.60s' and head-suite-head.log reads '3 failed, 180 passed in 212.30s' with the identical failure ids test_a_paired_dispatch_hides_each_arm.py::test_the_primary_arm_cannot_read_the_shadows_session_directory, test_crew_promotion.py::test_a_successful_store_write_is_reported_written_on_the_command_payload and test_*_payload, so the delta is zero added failures.

findings.text: _ledger_row_is_written duplicates the run-row scan that _ledger_holds_row at :2304 already owns, differing only in which ledger read it uses and what an unreadable store answers, so a future change to how a committed row is proven has to be made in two places; a single helper parameterised on the unknown-store policy would extend the owner instead of forking it.

assert comment['requested_narrative'] == retried compares the receipt's echo of the outcome the test itself passed into the call, so it holds for any implementation that reflects its input and cannot catch a regression in the behaviour under test; the case's durable guards are the kept_narrative assertion at :168 and the comment-body assertions at :172-174.

the refusal this change keeps for a differing narrative before a ledger row exists has no test, and neither does the unreadable-ledger arm that answers False at :2340, so reinstating a permissive path there would not redden any assertion even though the module docstring at :1453-1461 and the evidence fragment state the refusal as behaviour.

_narrative_text is applied to existing_body and requested_body, both already passed through html.unescape at :1450-1451, so the receipt's note unescapes a second time and would report text containing a literal entity such as '&lt;' as '<', which is not what the landing comment holds.
